turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Who decided that?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in, Hale. Was he heard before you decided?
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
You'll have it. Whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears about it. And you skipped my question about whether Owen was heard first.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
A wrong citation is a citation error, and seventeen-year-olds make them. That's twice now you've stepped around whether Owen was heard before the zero went in.

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.

I never said December 1, but it's the right date. Your own procedure, private, nothing on his record: he'll do it, to put this behind him. Tonight's email has all of it, the apology, and a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first.
Yes. Thursday, in your room, and nobody else in it but the two of you.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday, privately in your room, that you will mark it by Monday so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and that nothing goes on his record. I still expect your apology for entering the zero before contacting me, and a direct answer on whether Owen was heard before that zero was entered. I expect all of this in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, marked by Monday, with nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight with an apology and a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the dated version history with exact times and then answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by offering to check that other file's dates, which gave her something specific she could verify herself.
What cost ground: You twice stepped around her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero, which kept her focused on procedure and made her trust you a little less.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night, though it proves nothing about the essay and is only why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer it plainly with what happened and when, before you bring in the Hamlet citation.
